about_blocks.text: Sobriety.ca Foundation: a small residential rehab between Ottawa and Montreal
about_blocks.html: Sobriety.ca Foundation: a small residential rehab between Ottawa and Montreal

about_blocks.text: Sobriety.ca Foundation is a not-for-profit that runs a live-in addiction treatment centre called Sobriety Home. Its admissions office is on the 11th floor of 343 Preston Street in Ottawa, but treatment does not happen there. The residence is a converted farm property on Route 138 in Godmanchester, Quebec, near Huntingdon in the Haut-Saint-Laurent. The centre puts the drive from Ottawa at under two hours, and Montreal is about an hour away.

about_blocks.text: The house takes no more than 12 clients at a time, all adults 18 and over, and each one gets a private room with a private bathroom. People come for alcohol, drugs, prescription medication and gambling. You can refer yourself without a doctor's letter, and the centre also accepts pets, which is rare for a residential program.

People come for alcohol, drugs, prescription medication and gambling. You can refer yourself without a doctor's letter, and the centre also accepts pets, which is rare for a residential program.

about_blocks.text: Care runs in three stages. New arrivals who need it go through medical detox on site, which averages about seven days. A short rest period of up to 48 hours follows for anyone who is stable but worn out, and then the core treatment program begins. That program usually lasts at least 30 days and can run longer. A registered nurse works on site, a local physician sees every resident once a week, and a consulting psychiatrist handles concurrent conditions such as depression, anxiety and PTSD. The physician can prescribe anti-craving medication, including methadone and Suboxone.

about_blocks.text: Individual therapy is required for everyone. Group sessions are suggested case by case, and family and spousal counselling are offered as well. The centre describes its approach as non-12-step and medical-psychological, built on CBT, DBT, psychodynamic and trauma therapy, with SMART Recovery and an introduction to the 12 steps for those who want it. Yoga, massage, art therapy and an on-site gym fill out the days. Women sleep in a separate house from the men and have women-only sessions, while most groups are mixed.

about_blocks.text: After discharge, graduates get an exit plan and access to online aftercare groups led by trained facilitators. The centre says it keeps in touch with clients and their families for more than a year. Fees are not published, so call 1-888-999-8101 to ask about rates and payment. Note that Sobriety.ca Foundation is a different organization from Sobriety House, the men's recovery home on First Avenue in Ottawa.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Sobriety.ca Foundation

faqs.question: Where does treatment at Sobriety.ca Foundation actually take place?

answer_blocks.text: Treatment takes place at Sobriety Home, a residential centre on Route 138 in Godmanchester, Quebec, near Huntingdon. The 11th floor office at 343 Preston Street in Ottawa is the foundation's admissions office, not a treatment site. The residence is under two hours from Ottawa by car and about an hour from Montreal.

faqs.question: Is Sobriety.ca Foundation residential or outpatient?

answer_blocks.text: It is a residential program: you live at the Godmanchester house for the length of your stay. Detox happens on site, and aftercare after discharge is online. The centre's recent articles also mention online therapy and outpatient options, so ask admissions what is available if you cannot leave home.

faqs.question: Is Sobriety.ca Foundation the same as Sobriety House in Ottawa?

answer_blocks.text: No. Sobriety House is a separate men's recovery home at 90 First Avenue in Ottawa. Sobriety.ca Foundation is a different not-for-profit whose treatment centre, Sobriety Home, is in rural Quebec. The two have similar names but are not connected.

answer_blocks.text: The centre does not publish its prices. Its admissions page asks you to contact the team directly about rates and payment. It is a private-pay program, and it accepts major credit cards, personal cheques and bank drafts.

faqs.question: How do I get to the residence?

answer_blocks.text: You can drive in, or staff can pick you up anywhere within 100 kilometres of the centre. They also collect people from airports and train stations. For flights inside Canada the centre suggests Montreal-Trudeau Airport; from the US, Burlington and Plattsburgh airports and nearby Amtrak stations are options. The house is about ten minutes from the New York state border.

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Women sleep in a separate house away from the men's quarters and have access to women-only group sessions. Most therapy groups are mixed, which the centre says helps people prepare for life back home. Counsellors are trained to work with trauma, including sexual and physical violence.
